subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept SQLite-backed sha256/size provenance as the trust lifecycle for generated HTML after outbound media staging?
rationale: The code path appears fail-closed and well tested, but this is an intentional expansion of a local HTML host-read boundary and cannot be approved solely by automation.

options.title: Accept provenance lifecycle
options.body: Approve the content-bound outbound_media_provenance design and allow the PR to proceed through normal merge gates.

options.title: Require tighter cleanup bounds
options.body: Ask for TTL or chunked pruning hardening before merge if row growth and pathological cleanup cost are unacceptable.

options.title: Keep temp-root-only trust
options.body: Reject the trust expansion and keep this bug open for a different delivery design that avoids trusting staged HTML.

recommendation.title: Accept provenance lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve the content-bound outbound_media_provenance design and allow the PR to proceed through normal merge gates.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read seam and have the strongest traced history on the affected media/channel boundary.
